title: Megold vagy Megoldódik? Solving a Problem

sections.title: Someone solves it, or it just gets solved
sections.content: megold ("to solve") is a transitive verb — it needs someone doing the solving, and it agrees with its object the definite/indefinite way you already know: Megoldom a problémát. ("I'll solve the problem", a specific one, definite.) megoldódik ("to get solved") is its -ik-verb partner — no one is named as responsible, the problem itself is just the subject, the same shift you saw with elromlik back in this unit.

items.english: In the end, everything got solved.

sections.content: Use megold when you want to name who's doing the solving; use megoldódik when you just want to say the problem worked itself out, with no one singled out — the same kind of pattern as elromlik, where the broken thing is the subject and no one is blamed for breaking it.
